glosses: enfilade (gunfire directed along the length of a target)
ciąg pomieszczeń ułożonych jedno za drugim, połączonych przejściami umieszczonymi w jednej linii

examples.text: W naszym mieszkaniu są trzy pokoje w amfiladzie, dlatego trudno je sprzedać.

glosses: A line or straight passage, or the position of that which lies in a straight line.

examples.text: In his Booker Prize-winning novel The Line of Beauty, Alan Hollinghurst wrote about people who know their world history as being able to look back through the millennia as an enfilade of rooms: Greece yields to Rome; Rome to the Byzantine Empire ... the Renaissance ... the British Empire ... America ... China. The same goes for people who can recite their kings and queens. British history clicks into a long enfilade of discrete, identifiable periods.

glosses: Gunfire directed along the length of a target.

examples.text: Uncle Charles, a truly unparalleled slinger of shit, is laying down an enfilade of same, trying to mollify men who seem way more in need of a good brow-mopping than I.
In minutes they had gained the top, fell prone, and began to pour deadly repeater-fire into the enemy below while their compatriots raked the top of the coulee with an enfilade.

glosses: A series of doors that provide a vista when open.
To rake (something) with gunfire.

examples.text: A great quantity of artillery was placed upon the eminence, so as to batter and enfilade the left of their intrenchments.

As they scrambled up a narrow path they every where found holes dug to cover the defenders of the mountain, and sticks crossed for resting their guns, with which they enfiladed every angle, that from the steepness it was necessary to make in ascending.
It was by his order the shattered leading company flung itself into the houses when the Sin Verguenza were met by an enfilading volley as they reeled into the calle.
He killed the machine gun crew, and without further orders pushed on and enfiladed a ditch from which three officers and 160 men subsequently surrendered.

glosses: To be directed toward (something) like enfilading gunfire.

examples.text: Together they saw the market thicken, and in course of time thin away with the slow decline of the sun towards the upper end of town, its rays taking the street endways and enfilading the long thoroughfare from top to bottom.
From her rocking chair in the parlour, Mrs. Zell’s scrutiny enfiladed the entire block.

glosses: To arrange (rooms or other structures) in a row.

examples.text: […] the house had been boldly planned with a ball-room, so that, instead of squeezing through a narrow passage to get to it (as at the Chiverses’) one marched solemnly down a vista of enfiladed drawing-rooms (the sea-green, the crimson and the bouton d’or), seeing from afar the many-candled lustres reflected in the polished parquetry […]

glosses: Suite de pièces d’un appartement.

examples.text: En ornant la façade, il contribuait à donner des dégagements aux pièces d’enfilade.
Je poussai d'un coup de pied la porte de la salle à manger, à demi éclairée, comme le salon d'enfilade, par les vitrages donnant sur la serre.

glosses: Suite ou série longue et ennuyeuse.

examples.text: Une longue enfilade de phrases, d’épithètes.
C’est comme si ce président qui déteste par-dessus tout perdre s’infligeait à lui-même une enfilade de défaites assurées par pur masochisme.
Les skis sur le dos, nous longeâmes une enfilade de détaillants : l’empire du discount.

glosses: Action de tirer des coups de canon sur une troupe, une fortification, un navire dans le sens de leur longueur.

examples.text: Donner, recevoir une enfilade.
Tirer des coups d’enfilade.
Prendre en enfilade.

glosses: Meuble composé d’au moins trois éléments à la suite l’un de l’autre et sur le même plan.
Situation dans laquelle une pièce attaque deux pièces alignées où la pièce ennemie de plus grande valeur fait l’objet de l’attaque directe, à la différence d’un clouage.
Suite de messages consécutifs portant sur un même objet.

examples.text: D'un point de vue technique, on parle d'une enfilade, comportant un message initial portant x en objet, suivi de n messages portant Re: x.

glosses: архит. ряд примыкающих друг к другу помещений, дверные проёмы которых расположены по одной оси, что создаёт сквозную перспективу интерьеров

examples.text: Главной в планировке дома была анфилада парадных комнат, выходящая окнами на улицу.

перен. последовательно чередующийся ряд событий (о жизненном пути)
